notes: Every name below is a frozen contract proposal for S2/S3, not a claim that the API exists today.
Field lists are normative: an implementation that renames or drops one of them must revise this fixture in the same commit.

rules: DeclaredTypeFullNames records only the types the artifact itself declares or generates; referenced DTO/enum/contract types must never be mixed in
CCCRUD008 reconciles DeclaredTypeFullNames with CrudArtifactEmitter.DeclaredTypeFullNames(artifact.Source); mixing a referenced type is a hard diagnostic, not a naming preference

ReferencedTypeFullNames records referenced type identities separately, as plain FQNs; each entry resolves to exactly one definition by symbol identity (assembly + full metadata name + closed generic arguments)
OwnerAssemblyName is the HTTP glue owner; ContractAssemblyName and ReferencedTypeFullNames are sibling fields, never encoded as owner:type
ContentHash is 'sha256:<hex>' and is the write-if-changed and provenance key

properties: same inputs in any declaration order produce the same identity
two front ends claiming one artifact or action is a diagnostic, not a last-wins
an unrelated manifest hit must not suppress a whole assembly's legacy output

stages: one CoreCompile with the official STJ generator and all other generators
manifest.stageRule: ordering is an explicit DependsOn edge list, never BeforeTargets luck

forbidden: referenced DTO or contract FQN inside DeclaredTypeFullNames
owner/contract/referenced types concatenated into one string
ownership.evidence: reviewer ownership contrast 2/2: mixing a referenced type into DeclaredTypeFullNames triggers CCCRUD008

requiredJsonRoots.derivedFrom: the frozen action model, not a hand written table
categories: no-input actions (explicit no-input, never arbitrary object)
resource-not-found and failure DTOs owned by Web
scalar inputs that are serialized at run time
forbidden: one shared object envelope for all list shapes
reflection fill-in for a missing root

failureBridge.adapter: Web/Platform scoped adapter reuses the existing ICrestExceptionConverter with the real HttpContext
failureBridge.binderRule: normalise to InvalidRequest inside the typed binder, before handler entry; do not globally remap JsonException/FormatException because serialization failures on the response path are internal errors
failureBridge.singleNotFoundShape: CrestErrorResponse from the Web owner; the legacy DynamicApiResponse 404 wrapper stays in the legacy snapshot only
failureBridge.cancellationRule: caller abort and managed deadline keep their existing semantics; a classifier must not convert them into OperationInvalid and must not re-run business work

cancellation.principle: classify by the original cancellation source (R = RequestAborted, K = managed kernel/deadline token, L = linked), never by whether L is canceled; response suppression is decided separately from classification

cases.detect: only R canceled (identity resolves to R or to L with R canceled)
cases.http: no JSON error body; connection aborted if response not started; never rewrite a started response
cases.uow: abandon/rollback uncommitted per #137; committed stays committed

cases.detect: only K canceled while R is alive (identity resolves to K or to L with R not canceled)
cases.http: 500 Crest.InternalError, sanitized, only if the response has not started; otherwise abort without a second write
cases.uow: preserve Unknown/Committed facts; never rewrite them as a successful rollback

cases.detect: OCE token is a third token or None; never remapped by transport state
cases.uow: internal failure path; rollback if uncommitted
forbidden: treating it as caller cancellation and dropping the response

cases.detect: classification as above, but the committed fact wins
cases.http: no rewrite of the committed outcome
cases.uow: Committed preserved; notification failure does not roll back

cancellation.syncCall: sync and async kernel entries share the same classifier
cancellation.bindingStage: the same classifier applies at binding/validation: OCE(R) -> CallerAbort with no business, no transaction and no body; OCE(K) -> ManagedDeadline with a sanitized 500 when the response has not started; third token or None -> NonCaller with a sanitized 500; ordinary binding failures keep the converter's authority
cancellation.classificationFailure: unknown token identity falls back to a sanitized 500

tokens.L: linked token handed to business (R linked with K)

classification: 0. OCE.Token is default/None -> NonCaller; identity absence is established before any equality matching, otherwise a default OCE matches R when R is None and is misread as CallerAbort
1. OCE.Token == R -> R is canceled ? CallerAbort : NonCaller
2. OCE.Token == K -> K is canceled ? ManagedDeadline : NonCaller
3. OCE.Token == L -> R canceled ? CallerAbort : K canceled ? ManagedDeadline : NonCaller; when both are canceled CallerAbort wins and both sources are recorded
cancellation.precedence: when R and K are both canceled and the identity resolves to L: CallerAbort wins for classification and response suppression, while CallerAbort+Deadline is recorded as the fact set
cancellation.responseSuppression: suppress the body whenever R is canceled or the response has started, regardless of classification; otherwise write per classification (CallerAbort never writes a body; ManagedDeadline/NonCaller -> sanitized 500 Crest.InternalError)
edgeRules: None is handled before identity matching so a tokenless OCE is never attributed to a None-valued R
an identity match only classifies when the matching source is actually IsCancellationRequested; a handmade OCE carrying R/K without that source canceled is NonCaller
L with neither R nor K canceled is NonCaller, never a default ManagedDeadline
when R and K are the same token or L equals R (K not cancelable), attribute through the R check and record R==K without double counting

invariants: exactly one UnitOfWorkProviderBinding per ORM provider in the final graph
duplicate or missing binding is a startup diagnostic, before the first request
the test fixture is not an ownership participant
#137 deterministic rejection for genuinely different bindings stays in place

rules: definitions come from an explicit IPermissionDefinitionProvider in the sample, not a generated string table or seeded grant rows
no OR/alias fallback in the checker between Helpdesk.Tickets.* and Ticket.*
a Search or read grant is never auto promoted to Update

mustNotReference: an analyzer package containing the default formal generators

edges.sampleOptIn: explicit per owner/action allowlist recorded in the archive table

ids.CCHTTP003: owner, route, action or identity conflict
ids.CCHTTP004: json input, output or error closure incomplete
ids.CCHTTP005: formal path uses legacy or publishes the same action twice
ids.CCHTTP006: transport, manifest, stamp or path state invalid
ids.CCHTTP007: required host composition, validation or error contract missing
ids.CCHTTP008: action permission, kind, cancellation token or concurrency declaration contradicts

diagnostics.collisionCheck: repo-wide grep for CCHTTP recorded zero hits on 2026-10-17; re-checked before implementation

referencedAssembly.decision: declaration lives in the compiling HTTP owner; the contract (and its DTOs) may live in a referenced assembly
referencedAssembly.anchor: local marker class (may be static) carrying CapabilityCompatibilityProjection(ContractType = typeof(IX), RegistrationMode = ExplicitHost); no CrestService required in this mode
rules: ContractType is an accessible closed interface; only it and its inherited interfaces contribute methods
the marker class is never DI-registered or instantiated and its own public methods are not projected
existing facades that implement the contract keep today's behaviour; business DI stays with the owning module
the contract must be registered by the business owner; missing registration is a startup CCHTTP007, not a request-time 500
two HTTP owners declaring the same contract is CCHTTP003
artifact identity includes contractAssemblyName and the closed method signature; owner and contract stay separate fields
forbidden: scanning referenced assemblies for CrestService/projection attributes
same-short-name type stubs standing in for referenced contracts or DTOs
jsonClosure: referenced DTOs must appear as JsonSerializable roots and in official STJ metadata
same-short-name types across assemblies must not cross owners
generation must not write into the referenced assembly output

probes.R-01: a projection declaration inside a referenced assembly is not discovered by the consuming compilation
probes.R-02: ContractType mode enumerates only the contract surface
probes.R-04: missing contract DI registration fails at startup with CCHTTP007
probes.R-05: identity includes contractAssemblyName and no cross-assembly owner bleed
probes.R-06a: caller abort: no JSON error body, business observed cancellation once, no re-execution, #137 abandonment facts
probes.R-06b: managed deadline: sanitized 500 when the response has not started; Unknown/Committed facts preserved
probes.R-06c: non-caller OCE: treated as an internal fault (sanitized 500), never dropped as cancellation
probes.R-06d: linked-token identity resolution: deadline-only never hits CallerAbort; both canceled -> CallerAbort with both sources recorded
probes.R-06e: binding/validation uses the same classifier: OCE(R) no body, OCE(K) sanitized 500, third token/None sanitized 500
probes.R-06f: boundary: None before identity matching (R=None must not turn a default OCE into CallerAbort); identity match without the source canceled -> NonCaller; L with N/R/K untouched -> NonCaller

acceptanceMatrixDelta.H02: binding-stage cancellation follows the same classifier (OCE(R) no body; OCE(K)/third token -> sanitized 500), never a stage-wide attribution
acceptanceMatrixDelta.H07: R-06a-e: caller abort / managed deadline / non-caller OCE / both-cancel precedence / binding-stage same rule; fixed HTTP and #137 facts; cancellation never re-executes
acceptanceMatrixDelta.N01/N02: native gate adds one caller-abort and one non-caller OCE scenario
acceptanceMatrixDelta.D01: migration guide states the two client-visible cancellation behaviours
